column14: Heinl says "would augment" (plan of mid-May). CINCPAC's report (28 June, para 7) says "a part of the 2nd Raider Battalion with special equipment for meeting a mechanized landing assault"; ONI says the same.

rations: Five light tanks
a platoon of five light tanks
column14: Five tanks; men in the platoon not stated. The platoon arrived on the USS Kittyhawk 26 May as "the light tank platoon so urgently needed for the mobile reserve". Men in a tank platoon not stated.

rations: Each of the 22d and 23d Provisional Marine Companies included a weapons platoon armed with 81-mm and 60-mm mortars, light machine guns and old-type 37-mm guns
Each company included a weapons platoon armed with 81-mm and 60-mm mortars, light machine-guns and old-type 37-mm guns.
column14: The companies "provided interior security, beach patrols by night and a small mobile reserve"; counts of mortars or men not given. This row stands for both companies.

rations: First Lt. Thomas E. Clarke; Capt. Boyd O. Whitney
Commanding Officer, 23d Provisional Marine Company | First Lt. Thomas E. Clarke | Commanding Officer, 23d Provisional Marine Company | Capt. Boyd O. Whitney
column14: The staff list prints "23d Provisional Marine Company" twice, with a different officer each time; one of them presumably commanded the 22d. Which is which is not stated; this row is entered on the 23d and the other officer is not entered on the 22d.

rations: us-6th-defense-battalion
In addition to the above duties, they carried on intensive night battle training.
column14: The report (by the battalion commander) praises "The 22d and 23rd Provisional Infantry Companies" for unloading ships, making obstacles and mines, beach patrolling and interior guard; the staff list heads them under the 6th Defense Battalion (reinforced). The quotation is the end of that paragraph; the first part names the companies on the preceding lines.

rations: The ground crews of VMF-221 and VMSB-241 were the reserve (alerted about 0400 on 4 June when the transports were reported about 70 miles away); Kimes had a staff of a few officers; new pilots from the Kittyhawk had little flying time; in Dec 1941 the VMF-221 ground echelon was 3 officers and 110 enlisted
I thought it would be well to alert the reserves (ground crews of VMF-221 and VMSB-241).
column14: Kimes wrote after the battle. The 1941 figure is Ch. 3 p. 17 ("an aviation contingent of three officers and 110 enlisted Marines (the ground echelon of VMF-221)"), outside the period; no May 1942 strength of the ground echelon was found (gaps.csv). The alert time "about 0400" is Midway local (zone +12) as Kimes gives it.

rations: Capt. Cyril T. Simard, USN
C. T. SIMARD Captain. U.S.N. Commanding.
column14: The NAS commanding officer; Heinl (Ch. 1 p. 8) says the Naval Air Station was commissioned on 1 August 1941 under his prospective command, later promoted captain by Nimitz.

Transferred to this station this date: 20 rates, 33 non-rates, one Junior Grade Lieutenant.
column14: 20 rated men + 33 non-rated + 1 junior-grade lieutenant = 54 transferred in on 16 May (arrived on USS Sirius and Chandler). On 18 May "Transferred this date from this station: 17 rates, 6 non-rates" (23 out), so the net is 31. The station's total Navy strength is not stated (gaps.csv). Zone +12 (Midway local).

rations: Maj. Gen. Tinker (commanding the 7th Air Force) arrived by B-17 on 26 May with Maj. Warner of the Army Air Corps, who stayed with Marine Air Group 22 as liaison officer to the 7th Bomber Command; four B-26s with Army crews arrived 29 May; 17 B-17s and 4 B-26s were at Midway on 3 June
Major Warner of the Army Air Corps who will remain with Marine Air Group 22 to act as liaison officer between the 7th Bomber Command and Commanding Officer, N.A.S. Midway.
column9: https://midway1942.com/docs/usn_doc_12.shtml [War diary 1-29 May 1942, entries 26 May 1245 and 29 May 1315]
column14: Zone +12 (Midway local). The 3 June aircraft count is ONI chapter 2 p. 5 (quoted in the place_facts rows). No Army personnel strength found: Heinl (Ch. 1 p. 9) has only the October 1941 Signal Corps detachment of "one officer and four enlisted radiomen"; see gaps.csv.

The actual landing on Midway was to be accomplished by approximately 1,500 Special Naval Landing Force troops who would storm Sand Island; and by 1,000 Army troops of the Ikki Detachment
column9: https://www.ibiblio.org/hyperwar/USMC/USMC-M-Midway/USMC-M-Midway-3.html [Ch. 3 p. 22 (page marker 22), citing USSBS Nav No. 60 (Capt. Toyama, 1 Oct 1945) and "Japanese Land Forces No. 2", JICPOA translation 20 Oct 1942]
column14: 1,500 + 1,000 = 2,500, the sum of two figures Heinl gives, for the assault troops. Disputed: Japanese Monograph 93 gives 2,800 (2nd Combined SNLF) + 3,000 (Ikki) = 5,800 (the plan) and "approximately 2,000" and "approximately 3,000" in its prisoner-data annotation; Wikipedia gives "about 5000". Plan, not men landed. Heinl's quotation spans a page break and a footnote marker; the exact fragment is "by approximately 1,500 Special Naval Landing Force troops who would storm Sand Island; and by 1,000 Army troops of the Ikki Detachment, to land[ 16 ] on Eastern Island".

The 2 Combined Special Landing Party (two battalions, approximately 2,800 men) and the Ikki Detachment of the Army (one battalion, approximately 3,000 men commanded by the regiment commander)
column9: http://www.ibiblio.org/hyperwar/Japan/Monos/pdfs/JM-93_MidwayOperations,May-June42/JM-93.htm [Japanese Monograph 93, V.A.1.c "Actions of Various Units", p. 7]
column14: 2,800 + 3,000 = 5,800 for the two bodies, the plan as the Combined Fleet's Pacific Eastern Front plan states it (the monograph's own words "one battalion, approximately 3,000 men" are not consistent). Disputed with the Heinl 2,500 and the annotation figures. Does not count the construction units. Tokyo time (zone -9) is the monograph's clock; no clock for the figures themselves.

will depart from SAIPAN on the evening of 28 May
column14: The plan, "guarded by 2Sd and 7S". Heinl (Ch. 3 p. 25) says the amphibious shipping and the landing force "sailed from the Marianas two days later on 28 May" (a repeat of the plan's date; the 26 May is Nagumo's sortie). Date as printed (Combined Fleet central time); evening of 28 May Tokyo-dated.

will carry out the landing on 7 June
column14: Landing date of the Occupation Force, Tokyo-dated (the plan says its time is Central Standard Time, TN Central Pacific time; the air attack on Midway was to be at 0130 on 5 June in the same dating, which was 0430 on 4 June at Midway, zone +12, the hour the raid actually began). So the landing is 6 June in Midway local date. The Kure seaplane unit was to occupy Kure on 6 June (Tokyo date). Marked disputed with Bates' "N-day, June 6th" (below) and the possibility that the two are the same day in two calendars; not settled here.

All forces and groups were to be in the above positions on N-day, June 6th.
column9: https://archive.org/download/battleofmidwayin00bate/battleofmidwayin00bate_djvu.txt [Bates, Midway (1948), p. 19, passage on the disposition of the forces under "Separate Sheet 1"; OCR text]
column14: Bates gives N-day as 6 June for the deployment of the forces ("Separate Sheet 1"), the day by which the main body, the Aleutian support group and the Second Fleet were to be in position; whether N-day was also the landing day is not said, and the date is in US (Midway) reckoning. The 7 June of Monograph 93, Tokyo-dated, is 6 June at Midway, so the two may agree. Clock not stated.

rations: Landing plan: the 2nd Combined SNLF to storm Sand Island and the Army Ikki Detachment to land on Eastern Island, from the south side, boats to the reef and rubber boats beyond; "plenty of equipment for a three months' occupation"; the occupation unit: 2 Combined SNLF, one construction battalion, one survey unit and one Army detachment; the Navy to defend after the occupation and the Army unit to withdraw one week after the capture
We were going to approach the south side (of Midway), sending out landing boats as far as the reef.
column9: https://www.ibiblio.org/hyperwar/USMC/USMC-M-Midway/USMC-M-Midway-3.html [Ch. 3 p. 22 (page marker 22), quoting Capt. Toyama, USSBS Nav No. 60]
column14: Toyama's remarks. The organisation of the occupation unit is in Monograph 93 (table of units, p. 17): "2 Combined SNLF, one construction battalion, one survey unit, one Army detachment", with the tasks "Capture SAND and EASTERN Islands" and "Make arrangements for camping at the base". The withdrawal of the Army one week after the capture is item 8 of the Army-Navy agreement in the same monograph (p. 4). The monograph says "one construction battalion" here and "11 and 12 Naval Construction Battalions" on 13 June.

rations: Detachment Commander Ikki (Colonel Kiyonao Ichiki)
Commander: Detachment Commander IKKI. [Kana characters not included in this document.]
column14: The agreement has "Forces: A nucleus of one infantry regiment." Heinl (Ch. 3, footnote 16) says "the Ikki Detachment mentioned here is the same one which was destined to be annihilated by Marines at the Battle of the Tenaru, 21 August 1942 on Guadalcanal ... sometimes referred to as the Ichiki Detachment because the Japanese characters for 'ikki' and 'ichiki' are identical". This entity is that body in its Midway form (existing key jp-ichiki-detachment is the Guadalcanal body, parent not stated; the Midway body is a nucleus of the 28th Infantry, one battalion with engineers and artillery per other sources); not merged.

by 1,000 Army troops of the Ikki Detachment, to land[ 16 ] on Eastern Island
column9: https://www.ibiblio.org/hyperwar/USMC/USMC-M-Midway/USMC-M-Midway-3.html [Ch. 3 p. 22 (page marker 22), citing USSBS Nav 60 and the Ikki Report (JICPOA, 20 Oct 1942)]
column14: Heinl: 1,000 Army troops. Disputed with Monograph 93 (about 3,000 in the plan and in the annotation "Strength: Approximately 3,000") and Wikipedia (about 5,000 troops for the whole transport group). Plan figure, not men landed.

Ichinoki Detachment CO: Maj Gen ICHINOKI Strength: Approximately 3,000.
column9: http://www.ibiblio.org/hyperwar/Japan/Monos/pdfs/JM-93_MidwayOperations,May-June42/JM-93.htm [Japanese Monograph 93, annotation "Data concerning the occupation unit" in the chronology, p. 56]
column14: Printed as "Ichinoki ... Maj Gen" (the commander was a colonel) and "Strength: Approximately 3,000". Same figure as in the plan (V.A.1.c, "one battalion, approximately 3,000 men commanded by the regiment commander"). Disputed with the 1,000 of Heinl; the monograph's "one battalion" at 3,000 men is on its face too large. The annotation's date is the late-May chronology; clock not stated.

rations: jp-midway-landing-force
During the landing and landing battle, the Army unit and the Naval landing party will carry out operations at the same point, and the senior commander will assume the command of the operation.
column14: After assembly at Saipan (about 25 May) the 2nd Fleet commander "will assume the command of the Army unit in regard to the operation" (para 7.a). The Army unit was dropped from the 2nd Fleet's command on arrival at Guam (13 June, chronology).

rations: Guam
the 2 special Naval Landing Force and the Ichiki Detachment arrived at GUAM, escorted by two destroyers and four patrol ships.
column14: The entry is at 1450 hours. The detachment "was expected to arrive at GUAM on the 13th or 14th, and was to be stationed there" and dropped from the 2nd Fleet's command on arrival (entry on p. 84). Clock: Tokyo time (zone -9) as the monograph keeps it (the monograph's stated time zone); the date as printed.

rations: Capt. Minoru Ota (printed "Maj OTA OTA, Minoru")
2 Special Naval Landing Fores: Commanding Officer: Maj OTA OTA, Minoru
column9: http://www.ibiblio.org/hyperwar/Japan/Monos/pdfs/JM-93_MidwayOperations,May-June42/JM-93.htm [Japanese Monograph 93, annotation in the chronology listing the occupation unit, p. 56]
column14: The rank is printed "Maj" and the name doubled ("OTA OTA"); Wikipedia (Midway order of battle) has Captain Minoru Ota. The printed text is kept; the clean reading is Ota Minoru, rank not settled.

The 2 Combined Special Landing Party (two battalions, approximately 2,800 men)
column14: Plan figure ("two battalions, approximately 2,800 men"); the same monograph puts "Strength: Approximately 2,000" in an annotation, and Heinl 1,500. The plan also says 2,800 "will remain" as the garrison. Disputed; not settled.

1 YOKOSUKA SNLF; 2 KURE SNLF. Strength: Approximately 2,000.
column9: http://www.ibiblio.org/hyperwar/Japan/Monos/pdfs/JM-93_MidwayOperations,May-June42/JM-93.htm [Japanese Monograph 93, annotation in the chronology, p. 56]
column14: The annotation names the units as printed ("1 YOKOSUKA SNLF; 2 KURE SNLF") and gives "Strength: Approximately 2,000". Disputed with 2,800 (plan) and Heinl 1,500.

The actual landing on Midway was to be accomplished by approximately 1,500 Special Naval Landing Force troops who would storm Sand Island
column14: Heinl: about 1,500 for the assault on Sand Island. Disputed with the two Monograph 93 figures (2,800 and 2,000).

rations: Planned garrison armament after the occupation: 94 cannons of various types, 40 machine guns, six type A midget submarines and five torpedo boats; in the middle of June and afterwards four more midget submarines, two quadruple torpedo tubes and twelve 20-cm guns
Ninety-four cannons of various types, 40 machine guns, six type A midget submarines, and five torpedo boats will be prepared.
column9: http://www.ibiblio.org/hyperwar/Japan/Monos/pdfs/JM-93_MidwayOperations,May-June42/JM-93.htm [Japanese Monograph 93, V.A.2 "Defense after the Occupation of MIDWAY", p. 8]
column14: A plan; none of it was landed. "Preparations have been made to send four additional midget submarines, two quadruple torpedo tubes, and 12 20 cm guns in the middle of June and afterwards." The 2,800-man 2nd Combined SNLF would remain as the garrison.

The 13 Destroyer Group departed from YOKOSUKA, escorting the Yokosuka 1 Special Naval Landing Force on 20 May.
column9: http://www.ibiblio.org/hyperwar/Japan/Monos/pdfs/JM-93_MidwayOperations,May-June42/JM-93.htm [Japanese Monograph 93, chronology of the Attack Unit, Concentration at Saipan, item (1), p. 57]
column14: Printed "Yokosuka 1" (the Yokosuka SNLF ordered with the 2nd Combined body); the monograph does not give a number to the SNLF. The Yokosuka 5th SNLF of the Guadalcanal files is a different body; not merged. Date as printed (Tokyo).

The 16 Destroyer Group departed from KURE escorting the Kure 2 Special Naval Landing Force on 19 May.
column9: http://www.ibiblio.org/hyperwar/Japan/Monos/pdfs/JM-93_MidwayOperations,May-June42/JM-93.htm [Japanese Monograph 93, chronology of the Attack Unit, Concentration at Saipan, item (2), p. 57]
column14: Printed "Kure 2". The JINTSU and a destroyer left Kure on 21 May (item 3), and the escort squadron was complete at Saipan on 24 May with the arrival of Jintsu (item 5).

rations: Guam
At 1450 hours, the 2 special Naval Landing Force and the Ichiki Detachment arrived at GUAM
column14: Same entry as the Ikki Detachment row; Tokyo dating, as the monograph keeps. Heinl says the occupation shipping sailed from the Marianas on 28 May.

rations: jp-midway-landing-force
Assault elements in the landing would be backed up by the 11th and 12th Construction Battalions plus miscellaneous base-development detachments.
column9: https://www.ibiblio.org/hyperwar/USMC/USMC-M-Midway/USMC-M-Midway-3.html [Ch. 3 p. 22 (page marker 22), citing the Ikki Report]
column14: Heinl names the 11th and 12th Construction Battalions; the existing key jp-11th-construction-unit is the Guadalcanal 11th Construction Unit of August 1942 (about 900 men per the 1st Marine Division report); whether it is the same unit is probable but not stated by any source read here. Not merged.

rations: Truk
The 11 and 12 Naval Construction Battalions, escorted by the 2 Destroyer Squadron (less too divisions) and a subchaser unit, arrived at TRUK at 1130 hours.
column14: Both battalions in one sentence; the same fact is in the 12th's row. They were therefore in the 2nd Destroyer Squadron's convoy, or its escort group, at Truk on 13 June, after the battle; the monograph's organisation of the occupation unit gives only "one construction battalion". Clock: Tokyo time as printed.

rations: jp-midway-landing-force
Assault elements in the landing would be backed up by the 11th and 12th Construction Battalions plus miscellaneous base-development detachments.
column9: https://www.ibiblio.org/hyperwar/USMC/USMC-M-Midway/USMC-M-Midway-3.html [Ch. 3 p. 22 (page marker 22), citing the Ikki Report]

rations: Truk
The 11 and 12 Naval Construction Battalions, escorted by the 2 Destroyer Squadron (less too divisions) and a subchaser unit, arrived at TRUK at 1130 hours.
column14: Same entry as for the 11th.

rations: Aboard 12 transport vessels discovered at 0600 on 3 June by a US patrol plane 600 miles southwest of Midway; nine B-26s attacked in the afternoon without loss; the group earlier, 28 May, sailed from Saipan; Bates lists 13 transports and supply ships; the monograph's table gives 16 transports in the escort-and-occupation unit; no men per ship given
At 0600 hours, our occupation forces (aboard 12 transport vessels) were discovered by an enemy patrol plane at a point 600 miles southwest of MIDWAY.
column14: Clock: Tokyo time (zone -9) as printed by the monograph, date as printed ("3 June"); the US reports date this sighting 3 June at about 0900 Midway time, not checked here. The counts of 12, 13 and 16 are not reconciled here: Bates lists "thirteen transports and supply ships" by name (Nankai, Zenyo, Goshu, Brazil, Argentina, Seigho, Azuma, Kirishima, Kano, No. 2 Toa, Keiyo, Akebono and Hokuruku Maru; spelled so by the OCR text); the monograph's table says "16 transports" and "one transport" for the support unit. No men per ship in any source read.

The 8th Independent rapid fire company joins the Ichiki Detachment for a total 2,507 men.
column14: Combinedfleet's Nankai Maru page; the number of men of the detachment once the 8th Independent rapid fire company joined at Moji, before sailing. Differs from rows 6941 (Heinl, about 1,000 Army troops) and 6942 (Japanese Monograph 93, about 3,000, a planned figure). The page gives no source for the 2,507. Combinedfleet is a compilation (grade B).

which consisted of 3,000 troops
column14: Wikipedia, article on Ichiki: his 28th Infantry Regiment 'which consisted of 3,000 troops' was assigned to assault Midway. Tertiary; names no source for the figure. Agrees with row 6942 (Monograph 93, about 3,000); differs from 6941 (Heinl, 1,000) and from the combinedfleet 2,507 row in this batch. One source with the Monograph figure's order of size, not independent of it as far as can be told.

rations: Zenyo Maru (detachment headquarters and main body); Nankai Maru (remaining elements: four infantry companies, one machine gun company, one infantry gun platoon, one engineer company, one antitank company)
ZENYO MARU carries the Ichiki Detachments headquarters and main body. NANKAI MARU carries the remaining elements of the task force built around Colonel Ichikis 28th Infantry: four infantry companies, one machine gun company, one infantry gun platoon, one engineer company, and one antitank company.
column14: Combinedfleet, Nankai Maru and Zenyo Maru pages (the same text on both pages; one source). They sailed from Ujina on 18 May and reached Saipan 25 May. No other source on file says which ships carried the Army detachment; Wikipedia's order of battle names no split. Entry text copied as the page prints it (page spells the commander Ichiki Kiyono / Kiyonao).

The transports carry 5,000 troops including an airfield construction unit, LtCol Ichiki's detachment and two battalions of Special Naval Landing Forces (SNLF).
column14: Combinedfleet, Zenyo Maru page: the transport group's troops, all parts together (construction unit, Ichiki Detachment, two SNLF battalions). Agrees in order with Wikipedia (about 5,000, row 5802) and with Monograph 93 for SNLF plus Army only if the construction units are left out (5,800, row 6935); disagrees with Heinl (2,500, row 6934). Combinedfleet names no source.

rations: Argentina Maru (816 Kure Naval Landing Force troops loaded 5 May 1942); Kiyosumi Maru (Kure No. 5 Special Naval Landing Force, loaded at Kure 9 May)
Loads ammunition, sake, general supplies and 816 Kure Naval Landing Force troops.
column14: Combinedfleet, Argentina Maru page for the 816; the Kiyosumi Maru page (entry 9 May: 'Begins loading heavy equipment and the Kure No. 5 Special Naval Landing Force for transport') names a 'Kure No. 5' force, where Monograph 93 has the 2nd Combined SNLF made of a Yokosuka 1st and a Kure 2nd SNLF. The Argentina and Brasil pages also say they carried 'elements of the 5th Special Naval Brigade'. Names are the pages' own; whether these are one force under different names is not settled here. The 816 is the part aboard Argentina Maru, not a unit total.

rations: Kiyosumi Maru (Kure No. 5 Special Naval Landing Force and heavy equipment, loaded at Kure from 9 May 1942)
Begins loading heavy equipment and the Kure No. 5 Special Naval Landing Force for transport.
column14: Combinedfleet, Kiyosumi Maru page. Name as the page prints it ('Kure No. 5'); see the note on the previous row. Eight men of the embarked Kure SNLF were wounded in the strafing of 3 June (same page).

rations: Azuma Maru (elements, embarked 19 May at Yokosuka); Keiyo Maru (the 11th Construction Unit, same convoy of 19 May); Hokuriku Maru (elements of the 11th and 12th)
Embarks elements of the 11th Construction Unit.
column14: Combinedfleet, Azuma Maru page (embarked at Yokosuka 19 May, convoy with Meiyo, Hokuroku and Keiyo Marus; disembarked at Truk 13 June). The Keiyo and Hokuroku pages say the same convoy 'carries the 11th Construction Unit' (see the next rows). The Azuma page names the 11th only; the Hokuroku page also names the 12th.

rations: Keiyo Maru (convoy of 19 May from Yokosuka carrying the 11th Construction Unit)
The convoy carries the 11th Construction Unit.
column14: Combinedfleet, Keiyo Maru page: the convoy (Meiyo, Azuma, Hokuroku and Keiyo) carries the unit; which ship held how many is not given.

rations: Hokuriku Maru (elements of the 11th and 12th Naval Construction Units)
HOKUROKU MARU carrying 11th and 12th Naval Construction Units elements
column14: Combinedfleet, Hokuroku (Hokuriku) Maru page. The page's 19 May entry: 'The convoy carries the 11th Construction Unit.'

rations: Kano Maru (elements of the 12th Construction Unit and related supplies); Hokuriku Maru (elements of the 11th and 12th)
KANO MARU carrying elements of the 12th Construction Unit and related supplies
column14: Combinedfleet, Kano Maru page (and the Hokuroku page for the 11th and 12th).

Embarks 650 men of the 12th Construction Unit.
column14: Combinedfleet, Kano Maru page: 650 men of the unit embarked at Kure on 19 May (Kano Maru sailed with Kirishima, Yamafuku and Toa Maru No. 2 Go). A part of the unit (the part aboard Kano Maru), not the unit's total; some of the unit was in Hokuriku Maru. Heinl's 1,000-man figure for construction troops is not on file under this key.

rations: Goshu Maru carried the equipment of a seaplane unit, base equipment, munitions and ground crews (the Third Air Group's, to follow the occupation of Midway)
GOSHU MARU carries the equipment of a seaplane unit, base equipment, munitions, and ground crews.
column14: Combinedfleet, Goshu Maru page. The same page quotes a decoded cipher of 13 May about 'the Third Air will load its base equipment and ground crews ... AF (Midway)' for Goshu Maru. No figure of men given.

Shannon’s garrison now numbered 2,138 Marines.
column9: https://worldwar2inreview.blogspot.com/2024/11/never-battle-like-midway.html [paragraph after "On 25 May Nimitz wrote them again"]
column14: A blog post reproducing a narrative history of Midway (the post gives no author or book in the text read; the passage reads like a popular history). Shannon's garrison is the Marine ground force under Col. Shannon (the 6th Defense Battalion with its attachments), 'now' after the 25 May postponement of D day to 3 June. Differs from CINCPAC's estimate of 26 May (rows 6901, 6902, 6907: 71 officers + 1,828 men + raiders 9 + 270 = 2,178 Marines). Not independent of a book not read; low.

Simard’s fliers and service troops numbered 1,494, of whom one thousand were Navy personnel, 374 were Marines and 120 Army.
column14: Same blog passage: 'one thousand' Navy among the 1,494 'fliers and service troops' under Capt. Simard; the 374 Marines are the air group (us-mag-22-ground-echelon-midway) and the 120 Army the Army detachment. Round figure.

Simard’s fliers and service troops numbered 1,494, of whom one thousand were Navy personnel, 374 were Marines and 120 Army.
column14: Same blog passage: 374 Marines among Simard's fliers and service troops. Taken to be the Marine air group's men (aircrew and ground echelon); the passage does not say which unit. Inferred assignment.

Simard’s fliers and service troops numbered 1,494, of whom one thousand were Navy personnel, 374 were Marines and 120 Army.
column14: Same blog passage: 120 Army among Simard's fliers and service troops. Assigned to the 7th Air Force detachment by inference (the Army aviation personnel at Midway).

rations: Present at Wake in June 1942: in the entry for 9 to 12 June the 65th Guard Unit with two torpedo boats and subchasers attacked enemy submarines west of Otorijima (Wake)
Attack upon these submarines by our 65 Guard Unit, No 4 and No 5 Torpedo Boats, and subchaser unit was successful.
column9: http://www.ibiblio.org/hyperwar/Japan/Monos/pdfs/JM-93_MidwayOperations,May-June42/JM-93.htm [Japanese Monograph 93, chronology table, entry under 9 June (the next date printed is 13 June), between page markers --83-- and --84--]
column14: The monograph writes OTORIJIMA, the Japanese name of Wake (Spennemann: Wake was renamed Ottori Jima on 22 December 1941; Marcus is "Minami Torishima" in the same monograph). The date is inside the 9 to 12 June span; the table prints no 10 to 12 June heading. This is the only June 1942 statement found of the garrison unit.

rations: 6th Base Force, Kwajalein (4th Fleet)
the occupation of Wake Island led to the establishment of an additional Naval Garrison Unit there, the 54 th Keibitai, which was considered to be more important and thus was made directly subordinate to the 6 th Base Force on Kwajalein
column9: https://marshall.csu.edu.au/Marshalls/html/Wake_WWII/Wake_WWII-Text.html [Spennemann, section "Command structure of the Japanese forces in the Marshall and Gilbert Islands", text above figure 6]
column14: Spennemann writes "54 th Keibitai" in this sentence and "65 th" everywhere else; the JACAR glossary gives the 65th and the hierarchy 4th Fleet, 6th Base Force, 65th Guard Unit, so the 54th is read as a slip. Valid for December 1941 to August 1942 as the figure 6 span he gives.

rations: 4th Fleet Headquarters > 6th Base Force > 65th Guard Unit (end of the war)
Combined Fleet ＞ 4th Fleet Headqurters ＞ 6th Base Force ＞ 65th Guard Unit
column9: https://www.jacar.go.jp/english/glossary_en/term/0100-0040-0110-0020-0010-0010-0020-0040.html [JACAR glossary, "65th Guard Unit", Upper level hierarchy]
column14: The place-and-time of the hierarchy is the end of the war; it agrees with Spennemann for 1942.

rations: Captain Sususmu Kawasaki, IJN (island commander from January 1942; relieved 13 December 1942 by Captain Shigematsu Sakaibara)
In January 1942 Captain Sususmu Kawasaki, IJN, was appointed island/atoll commander.
column14: Spelling as printed ("Sususmu"; probably Susumu, not shown). Under Admiral Kajioka at first. Wikipedia (Wake Island) says Sakaibara "arrived by aircraft to command Wake starting in December 1942", agreeing with the relief date.

65th Guard Unit (2,000 men), Captain Shigematsu Sakaibara
column9: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Structure_of_the_Imperial_Japanese_forces_in_the_South_Seas_Mandate [Wikipedia, "Structure of the Imperial Japanese forces in the South Seas Mandate", section "Wake Island Fortress", Japanese Navy units]
column14: Undated (the section is a late-war order of battle; Sakaibara commanded from December 1942, so after June 1942). The page lists "Total: 2,200 men" for the navy units. The article gives no citation for the figure.

The troop strength of the Wake Atoll garrison was approximately 2700 men by December 1942
